criterion: A numerical feature-by-injection abundance matrix is available
evidence: Complete MetaboLights and GigaDB inventories contain spectra plus ISA/readme files only; no matrix-like file exists.
consequence: Stop before preprocessing and correction methods.

criterion: The matrix represents uncorrected or minimally processed intensities
evidence: No matrix was deposited, so processing state cannot be assessed.
consequence: Cannot establish a valid benchmark input.

criterion: No run-order correction, batch correction, QC normalization, or destructive global scaling has already been applied
evidence: No matrix was deposited, so prior correction or normalization cannot be certified.

criterion: Study samples and pooled QCs are represented in the same feature matrix
evidence: Study and QC spectra coexist, but there is no shared feature matrix.
consequence: QC-based benchmarking is impossible without new peak processing.

criterion: Matrix columns can be matched unambiguously to injection metadata
evidence: ISA injections map to spectral files, but no matrix columns exist.
consequence: No safe matrix/metadata alignment is possible.

criterion: Five batches and within-batch acquisition order can be reconstructed
evidence: ISA-Tab provides complete unique batch/order pairs; batch sizes are 42,43,35,44,63 and the supplement corroborates the sequence.
consequence: Order metadata would be usable if a matching matrix were supplied.

criterion: QC identities and positions can be reconstructed
evidence: Sixty-six pooled QCs are explicit; per-batch counts are 13,14,15,13,11.
consequence: A constrained QC holdout would be feasible with a matrix.

criterion: Gestational classes can be assigned to study samples
evidence: A-F counts are 28,26,27,29,26,25; exact gestational week is unavailable and deposited F is 29-32 versus published 29-40.
consequence: Use A-F only unless precise weeks are supplied.

criterion: Every batch contains sufficient study samples for within-batch drift testing
consequence: Drift testing would be feasible after valid feature extraction.

criterion: Every batch contains enough QCs for QC-based competitor methods
consequence: QC-based competitors would have sufficient controls.

criterion: First and last usable QC positions can be retained for QC-RFSC
evidence: Every batch begins and ends with an observed QC.
consequence: Boundary QCs could be protected from holdout selection.

criterion: Gestational class is not severely confounded with batch or run order
evidence: All six classes occur in all five batches; chi-squared=14.684, df=20, p=0.794, Cramer's V=0.151; the published sequence is interspersed.
consequence: Randomization is acceptable for a future matrix-based benchmark.

criterion: The deposited data are not merely final normalized study values
evidence: Deposited mzML/mzXML spectra are upstream of normalization, but no derived abundance matrix is available.
consequence: Using spectra requires a newly authorized peak-picking and alignment workflow.
